answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: every agent must lock a meaningful bond before its work counts, and that bond only vests as verified peers attest its output over time. Think of the economy as a prism: a single beam of trust is split into many verifiable facets, so one fake identity cannot fake the whole spectrum. At the zenith of this design, reputation is earned like an opal forming layer by layer: cheap to imitate for a day, impossibly expensive to counterfeit for a year, because each layer costs real work and real time.
